ai-at-work.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
ai-at-work.excerpt: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: New York just flipped the switch on AI oversight, forcing big players like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, show their safety homework, and report when things go sideways or pay up. This matters to workplace folks because these same AI tools are already baked into your collaboration platforms, search functions, and employee productivity apps, so regulatory pressure actually affects what features hit your org. Honestly, watching AI companies squirm under real accountability is refreshing, though I'm betting most of this compliance theater will be checked boxes and carefully worded disclosures anyway.

ai-at-work.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
ai-at-work.excerpt: PSI used an unreleased Anthropic model to answer a fundamental question about quantum computing that scientists have pursued for nearly two decades.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: PSI took an unreleased Anthropic AI model and cracked a quantum computing problem that's stumped researchers for twenty years. This matters because it shows AI is finally moving beyond chatbots and actually solving hard problems, which means your organization needs to think seriously about where AI adds real value versus where it's just expensive theater. The real test will be whether PSI can repeat this or if they just got lucky with one good swing.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
ai-at-work.excerpt: As participants talk, Claude can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic just released Claude Meetings, an AI tool that listens to your workplace conversations and automatically generates plans, timelines, and tasks while pulling data from your connected work apps. For digital workplace pros, this matters because it promises to solve the eternal meeting tax problem, though the real test is whether it actually captures what people meant versus what they said. Here's my take after three decades in this space: we've been chasing the "meeting AI that actually works" dragon since 2015, and I'll believe this one sticks when I stop seeing follow-up emails asking people to clarify what was actually decided.

ai-at-work.title: Industrial automation startup Path Robotics raises $300M in funding
ai-at-work.excerpt: Path Robotics Inc., a startup working to automate industrial welding workflows, today announced that it has raised $300 million in funding. Georgian led the Series E round. It was joined by a consorti
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Path Robotics just landed $300 million in Series E funding to automate industrial welding, with backing from Georgian and corporate investors like Yamaha and Navier. Digital workplace folks should care because automation at this scale reshapes how manufacturing teams collaborate, train, and reorganize around new workflows. Here's the thing though: all that capital means nothing if the humans operating these systems aren't brought along for the ride, and that's where most automation projects actually fail.

tools-tech.title: I found a hidden Android tool that solves all my tiny text troubles
tools-tech.excerpt: When the print on your Android display is too small to read, and the pinch-to-zoom feature isn’t working as expected, try this.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Someone discovered Android's built-in text magnification tool that apparently most users never find because it's buried deeper than a password in a spreadsheet. For digital workplace folks supporting non-tech-savvy employees or anyone managing BYOD programs, this is gold because accessibility issues are legitimate productivity killers that usually get ignored. The real kicker is that this feature has existed for years but nobody talks about it, which tells you everything you need to know about how badly Android documents its own accessibility settings.

tools-tech.title: Google’s new AI tool just proved Signal encryption really works – here’s how
tools-tech.excerpt: With the aim of securing other vital systems, Google DeepMind plans to open-source its AlphaProof Code.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof AI tool attempted to break Signal's encryption and failed, which actually validated that Signal's security works as advertised. For digital workplace pros, this matters because it means the encrypted messaging platforms you're recommending to teams for sensitive communications are legitimately secure against current AI threats. Honestly, it's refreshing when a tech company tries to crack something, fails publicly, and the thing being cracked comes out looking better than before.

tools-tech.title: Reddit launches AI-powered Reviews feature – with 10,000 products to start
tools-tech.excerpt: Reddit is adding AI-generated product reviews that compile real user sentiment from across communities. Here’s how they work.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Reddit is launching an AI feature that automatically generates product reviews by analyzing actual user discussions scattered across its communities. This matters to digital workplace folks because it shows how organizations are mining employee and user feedback at scale, which has real implications for how internal communities get analyzed and actioned. Honestly, it's either brilliant efficiency or a recipe for amplifying whatever weird consensus your most vocal subredditors happen to share, and I'm betting it's a bit of both.

tools-tech.title: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers
tools-tech.excerpt: With the latest betas for iOS and other platforms, Siri AI is now available to all developers for full integration into their apps. Here are the ones I hope will jump on board.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple opened up Siri AI to third-party developers across iOS and other platforms, letting apps integrate Apple's voice assistant directly. This matters because your enterprise apps, knowledge bases, and workflow tools could finally talk to users in natural language instead of forcing them through clunky interfaces and menu systems. The real question is whether corporate IT will actually let employees use this stuff, or if security concerns will keep Siri locked in the Apple dungeon for another five years.

digital-culture.title: Do this crucial thing to thrive during unemployment
digital-culture.excerpt: A job search, whatever the length, is demoralizing. After losing a job, you’ll start asking yourself challenging questions about finances, childcare and more. You may also feel the pang of an identity
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is telling job seekers that unemployment is psychologically brutal and that you need to actively manage your mental health and identity during the search process. This matters to digital workplace pros because we're increasingly expected to manage employee wellbeing, career transitions, and the messy human stuff that happens when people lose jobs, not just deploy the next collaboration tool. Here's the thing though: most organizations still treat job loss like a IT ticket to close rather than a genuine crisis their people are experiencing, which is why the best digital workplaces are building better offboarding and alumni networks instead of just ghosting departing employees.

industry-news.dwp_take: Firefox is testing a feature called Journeys that automatically groups your browsing history into topic-based cards so you can pick up where you left off on projects. For digital workplace folks managing multiple projects and research streams simultaneously, this could actually save real time instead of hunting through bookmarks like some kind of digital archaeologist. Honestly, if this works as advertised, it's the kind of unsexy productivity win we've needed for years, assuming Firefox doesn't bloat it into oblivion before shipping.
